mutants.description: Rolling min/max expires entries older than index - window, so it keeps window + 1 values.
Welford update adds delta squared to M2 instead of delta times (x - new mean).
quantile(q) forms the rank target as ceil(qn) with the epsilon n slack left out.
Welford accumulator returns the one-pass naive variance (sum of squares minus sum squared over n) instead of M2.
RollingMinMax.minimum reports the newest candidate at the back of the minimum deque, not the front.
QuantileSketch.quantile returns the first stored value whose running rank is strictly above the target rank.
WelfordAccumulator.variance swaps the population and sample divisors, so ddof 0 returns the sample variance.
QuantileSketch.quantile takes the floor of qn - epsilon n as the target rank, not the ceiling, so it can answer one rank early.
RollingMinMax.push expires the minimum deque only, so maximum() can report a value that has left the window.
WelfordAccumulator.update adds the squared deviation from the old mean to M2, which drops the (n - 1) / n factor of the update.
Rolling maximum uses the min-deque pop rule (pops while the back is at least x), so larger values are discarded.
Quantile sketch treats a value equal to the current maximum as a duplicate and does not store it.
Quantile reads the sorted values at index floor(q (n - 1)), the numpy-style index, instead of the rank target.
Quantile treats the interval for q as half-open at zero and raises for q = 0, though the page names [0, 1] as closed.
minimum() reads the newest entry of the minimum deque instead of its front, so it reports the latest value.
RollingMinMax(None) treats None as an unbounded window, so minimum() answers over every value pushed so far.
variance(None) is read as the default ddof 1 and returns the sample variance instead of raising.
variance truncates ddof to an int before it is compared, so a float ddof of 0.5 is answered as the population variance.
quantile rounds q to six decimal places before it forms the exact rank target, a student's float-noise guard that changes the target near a whole rank.
quantile(q) returns the value after the target rank: the scan uses rank > target, one stored value too far.
quantile(q) forms the rank target as ceil(qn) minus floor(epsilon n), a common shortcut that differs from the exact ceil(qn - epsilon n) when epsilon n is not whole.
variance(1) with one value added returns 0.0 instead of raising, so the named condition (2) is not refused.
Welford update returns at once on a False value, so the boolean is neither counted nor averaged.
RollingMinMax truncates a non-integral float window with int(), so the window 2.5 becomes 2.
QuantileSketch.add returns without adding a False value, as if it were not a number.
RollingMinMax.push ignores a True value, so a boolean never enters the window.
variance treats every string ddof as the sample divisor, so the string '2' is answered instead of refused.
variance reads a None ddof as 0 and answers the population variance instead of raising.
RollingMinMax reads a None window as a window of one, so the call answers instead of raising.
QuantileSketch.add silently skips a whitespace-padded string instead of refusing it or reading it.
variance answers a float ddof of 1.0 with the population variance, although 1.0 denotes the sample divisor.
RollingMinMax.push reads a whitespace-padded string as 0.0 instead of refusing it or reading the number.
count returns a float instead of an int.
Naive sum-of-squares variance (sum x*x minus n*mean*mean), not Welford's update.
count is writable, so a caller can change the number of values.
Sample variance divides by n (population divisor) instead of n - 1.
variance with a ddof other than 0 returns the sample variance instead of raising.
Rolling window keeps window + 1 values (expiry off by one).
Quantile rank target is floor(q n), which drops the epsilon n slack and rounds the rank down.
update accepts NaN when it is the first value.
Welford M2 increment is delta squared, the deviation from the old mean, not delta times the new deviation.
update prints each value it is given.
Quantile sketch add() accepts NaN without raising ValueError.
a window below one is silently raised to one instead of raising.
the minimum deque never expires its front, so an expired minimum is reported.
variance(1) raises with two values and only accepts three or more (edge case at count 2).
Monotonic deque never removes expired indices from its front, so expired extremes stay reported.
the sketch accepts epsilon equal to one.
quantile accepts q = +inf and answers as if q were one.
the rank target rounds to the nearest integer instead of up to the next one.
Quantile rank target is computed as ceil(q n - epsilon n) in 64-bit floats, not exact Fractions, so it can fall one rank short.
Quantile rank target uses q n + epsilon n, the slack added rather than subtracted, so the answer sits one slack too high.
Rolling min and max expire an index at window - 1 steps, so each window holds one value fewer than the window size.
Quantile computes the rank target in floats (q times n minus float epsilon times n), so it can fall one rank short.
Quantile takes the floor of qn minus epsilon n as the rank target, not the ceiling, so it can answer one rank early.
Quantile returns the first stored value whose rank is strictly above the target rank, one stored value too high.
Welford mean divides the deviation by count + 1 instead of count (off-by-one in the running mean).
Quantile rank target subtracts twice the slack, so the target falls one rank too low and the second inequality fails.
The rolling maximum drops its front index one step early, so a maximum that is still in the window is lost, while the minimum expires correctly.
quantile(1.0) returns the smallest stored value, a special case the student adds for the top of the range.
Welford update silently skips infinite values, so the mean and variance stay finite and no error is raised.
The sketch rejects a boolean epsilon with TypeError, although False and True need ValueError by name.
The sketch's add() ignores None without an error, so a None value that denotes no number is silently dropped.
The rolling minimum and maximum ignores a None pushed as a value, as if it were never pushed.
quantile() on an empty sketch raises IndexError instead of the ValueError that the specification names.
